newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar takes central bank hint, ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar takes central bank hint, ends lower.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower on Wednesday, taking the central bank's strong hint after Tuesday's close that it would not oppose a depreciation in view of the U.S. dollar's bold international rise, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at its intra-day low of T$27.508, against Tuesday's T$27.438 close.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$317.5 million.

The unit had edged lower through the day but it was only in the final minutes that it breached T$27.50 -- something dealers had said was highly likely even before the central bank comment due to the passing of an annual pre-lunar new year demand peak.
Central bank vice governor Liang Cheng-chin said on Tuesday the Taiwan dollar "in theory" should reflect the U.S. dollar's prolonged overseas rise.
Unlike many currencies, however, the Taiwan dollar has moved in lockstep with the U.S. dollar and even appreciated against the greenback in 1997.

Liang attributed the Taiwan dollar's persistent strength despite the U.S. dollar's sharp appreciation against the yen and other major currencies to "seasonal factors" -- a reference to strong demand for cash before the Chinese lunar new year.
Dealers said pre-holiday demand now had evaporated.
"Since the central bank has hinted (at a depreciation), anticipation on the Taiwan dollar suddenly strengthened as the pre-lunar new year demand ended today," said one dealer.
Dealers said the depreciation clearly reflected the U.S. dollar's strength in recent months, especially against the Japanese yen, a trend that continued on Wednesday in Tokyo.
They said active demand for U.S. dollars by Taiwan people preparing for overseas travel during the year's biggest holiday break helped to further undermine the Taiwan dollar's value.
Further Taiwan dollar depreciation is expected, with some dealers saying the rate would range around T$27.47-27.55 when trading resumes after the holiday.
The lunar new year shutdown lasts five days starting from Thursday, with trade resuming on Tuesday, February 11.
